title: The Lesson I Learned When Saul Built a Monument for Himself
paragraphs: The Lesson I Learned When Saul Built a Monument for Himself
1 Samuel 15:12
Saul was sent to obey God.
But instead, he built a monument.
Not an altar.
Not a place of repentance.
A monument.
To himself.
“Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself…” — 1 Samuel 15:12
Read that again.
God gave him a command, but Saul wanted a legacy.
God wanted obedience, but Saul wanted recognition.
And here’s the part that should make every lukewarm heart tremble:
Saul still looked religious.
He still talked like a servant of God.
He still claimed he obeyed.
But God saw it.
You knew.

You knew there were areas where obedience became negotiable.
You knew you were keeping parts of your old life alive while still saying, “Praise the Lord.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Partial obedience is still rebellion.
Samuel told Saul:
“To obey is better than sacrifice.” — 1 Samuel 15:22
God was not impressed by Saul’s excuses.
And He is not impressed by ours.

You can build a platform and lose your soul.
You can have applause and no surrender.
You can look chosen and still be rejected because pride replaced repentance.
Saul’s monument revealed his heart.
He wanted the benefits of God without the authority of God.
That is the danger.
Not that you fail.
But that you fail and still protect your image.
The Gospel does not call you to build a monument to yourself.
It calls you to die.
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
Jesus did what Saul refused to do.
He obeyed the Father completely.
“He humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.” — Philippians 2:8
And through His blood, sinners like us can be forgiven.
Not by works.
Not by image.
Not by religious performance.
But by grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
“By grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works, so that no one may boast.” — Ephesians 2:8–9
So tear down the monument.
Repent.
Stop defending what God told you to destroy.
Come to Jesus.
Because grace is not permission to stay proud.
Grace is power to become new.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
